free_tier.stated: No free tier. The pricing page lists three plans, Standard, Plus and Pro, and a 1 Week term at $2; no monthly or yearly rate was read from the captured text.
free_tier.notes: The price is the vendor's plan rate for the subscription whose exits are classified here; the exit-address measurement itself has no price.

per_object_cap.notes: The classified sample is 89 addresses over 22 ASNs; none of those numbers is an object size.

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
retention.notes: Nothing is stored, so no retention clock applies. How long one exit address is held before it is re-drawn was not observed.

egress.terms: unverified: no traffic allowance or per-GB price appears in the captured pages; metered is recorded false because no metered charge was read.

interface_detail: The server list at https://api.ivpn.net/v5/servers.json is the source of the exit addresses classified here. The schema interface enum has no token for a VPN tunnel, so the tunnel protocols are not recorded as an interface.
tooling: The exit addresses are read from https://api.ivpn.net/v5/servers.json and classified with an IP-class detector; the service itself is reached with the vendor's own client or a WireGuard or OpenVPN configuration.
chaining: A Worker or a free compute node dials the tunnel and the traffic leaves at one of these exit addresses, so the upstream sees an address in the ASNs listed here and not the caller's network.
binding_note: No limit kind binds the record: it measures exit addresses and states no byte quota or request rate. What matters is list membership: 81 of 89 sampled exits are on a datacenter list.

identity_cost.detail: The pricing page states no email is required for signup, with cash, Monero and Bitcoin accepted.

reliability_note: 81 of 89 sampled exit addresses are on a datacenter list and 89 of 89 on a VPN list, so a site that blocks those lists blocks most of this fleet; 1 of 89 are also on an abuse list.
confidence_note: The list membership, ASN spread and counts are measured: each address was answered by the detector at the stated index version. The plan price and the identity class are documented from the vendor's captured pages; where a page did not state them they are unverified. The sample is the addresses the vendor endpoint returned, not proof that every address a user is handed is in it.

evidence.proved: The vendor endpoint https://api.ivpn.net/v5/servers.json gave 89 IPv4 exit addresses, each answered by the address-class detector at index version 20261103T163900Z-00d117b2 on 2026-11-03. Datacenter list: 81 of 89; VPN list: 89 of 89 (23 in the x4b VPN list); abuse list: 1 of 89; on none of the three: 0 of 89. 22 distinct ASNs and 85 distinct /24s; largest ASN AS60068 CDN77 Datacamp Limited with 28 addresses.
Detector index version 20261103T163900Z-00d117b2 was the one every one of the 89 answers carries.
the pricing page lists a 1 Week term at $2 in USD

notes: List membership of 89 exit addresses (detector index version 20261103T163900Z-00d117b2, 2026-11-03): datacenter 81, VPN 89, abuse 1, none of the three 0. VPN list: 89 of 89, of which 23 are in the x4b VPN list and the rest are in the vendor's own server list as ingested by the detector, so the VPN count includes the vendor feed. Definitions: datacenter is an address inside a range the x4b datacenter list publishes; VPN is inside the x4b VPN list or a per-provider server list; abuse is on at least one independent abuse family; none of the three states list membership, not physical siting.

extras.rung_note: Addresses came from the vendor's own server list and each was classified; no exit was connected to, so the address a user is handed at connect time was not observed.
